extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, science journalists, and interested public tracking retractions and citation impact
extracted.subtask_description: Produce a top-10 ranking of retracted scientific papers based on citation counts, showing citations before and after retraction and a total citation count drawn from Web of Science. The list is presented as of a specific cutoff date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time cutoff / list date
rubrics_metrics.description: Below, we present the list of the 10 most highly cited retractions as of November 12, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ranking and counts are anchored to a specific date (Nov 12, 2025); figures reflect citations recorded up to that cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article (title, journal, publication date, authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry shows the article title along with the journal name and publication date and the full author list (as presented in the table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include bibliographic metadata so readers can identify the retracted work; this metadata is used to link citation counts to the specific article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year of retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Column labeled 'Year of retraction' indicating the year in which the article was retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to contextualize when the retraction occurred relative to citation accrual (helps separate pre- and post-retraction citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing Articles before retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Column labeled 'Citing Articles before retraction' showing the number of citing articles that occurred prior to the retraction date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates citations that accrued while the paper was still officially published from those that occurred after retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing Articles after retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Column labeled 'Citing Articles  after retraction' showing the number of citing articles that occurred after the retraction date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights ongoing citation of retracted work; the article notes that some papers received more citations after retraction, an ongoing problem documented in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cites (journals indexed by Web of Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Column labeled 'Total cites (journals indexed by Web of Science)' — the summed citation count reported in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology note: 'To obtain the number of citations before and after a retraction was issued, we relied on the “Citation index” portion of Clarivate Analytics’ Web of Science (WoS), which only adds up the number of citations from journals indexed by the WoS Core Collection. Therefore, the citation count using just those two values can be lower than the total citation count for each article listed by WoS.' The table's total is therefore limited to citations from WoS Core Collection journals and may undercount other citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation counting method / source
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Clarivate Analytics’ Web of Science 'Citation index' (WoS Core Collection) as the source for before/after citation tallies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly relying on WoS Core Collection means non‑WoS-indexed citations are excluded; the page altered column headings 'to better reflect the criteria causing the discrepancy in total counts.' Readers should interpret totals in light of WoS coverage limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of post-retraction citation behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting that some papers received more citations after they were retracted, e.g., the #8 most cited paper received more citations post-retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is raised as a substantive observation about the phenomenon (and a problem documented by research) rather than a numeric metric, but it functions as an evaluative criterion for assessing the ongoing impact and visibility of retracted work.
